government.note: Government type as on 1 January 2000: the 1990 Constitution gave the directly elected President wide executive powers (a semi-presidential system). President Franjo Tuđman had been incapacitated since 26 November 1999 and died on 10 December 1999; the Speaker acted as President. The constitutional amendments of November 2000 (completed in 2001) moved Croatia to a parliamentary system with a directly elected, non-partisan President (five-year term, two terms at most), and the Government headed by the Prime Minister has held executive power since; the type field keeps the 2000 value. The Chamber of Counties was abolished by a 2001 constitutional amendment, leaving a unicameral Sabor.

system.note: Since the January 2000 election: ten constituencies of 14 seats each (D'Hondt, 5% threshold per constituency), plus seats for voters abroad (3 under the current law) and 8 seats for national minorities, giving 151 seats (152 in 2003 and 153 in 2007). The 127-member chamber elected in October 1995 used a mixed system with diaspora and minority seats. Since 2001 this is the whole (unicameral) Sabor.

chambers.review_note: seats_2000 is the October 1995 result as shown in the election infobox (HDZ 75; HSS–IDS–HNS–HKDU–SBHS alliance 18, recorded under HSS; HSLS 12; SDP 10; HSP 4), with one second-round seat for IDS, the Serb People's Party (2) and Social Democratic Action (1) as others, and four minority members as independents. How the four joint-list seats were split between the infobox totals was inferred; mid-term changes up to 1 January 2000 were not checked.

system.note: Three members elected per county (and the City of Zagreb), plus up to five members appointed by the President. seats_2000 is the result of the April 1997 election (63 elected, 5 appointed). Abolished by the 2001 constitutional amendment.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the October 1995 Chamber of Representatives list vote (shares computed from the vote counts): HDZ 45.2% plus the Croatian Christian Democratic Party 0.7% (Christian democrat), the HSS–IDS–HNS–HKDU–SBHS alliance 18.3% (recorded as agrarian after its leading party), HSLS 11.6% (liberal conservative, the party's current classification), SDP 8.9%, Social Democratic Union 3.2% and Social Democratic Action 1.7% (social democrat), HSP 5.0% and HSP 1861 1.3% (ethno-nationalist), Croatian Independent Democrats 3.0% (centrist liberal); the remaining small lists (about 1%) are recorded as big tent. The 3 January 2000 election, two days after the start date, changed this balance sharply.
